hero.definition: Imbustai is a story you live by post. The characters write you real letters that arrive at your home. You reply in your own words, and the story changes with what you write.
hero.envelopeFrom: From someone you don’t know yet

facts.label: Imbustai in short
values: A tale told by correspondence. You don’t read it: you’re in it.
One complete story. The letters arrive at your home, one at a time.
A mystery to live slowly: you wait, open, reply. And the plot moves with you.

steps.title: How it works, in four moves
bodies: Each story has its own world, its characters and a secret.
Envelope, stamp, postmark. In your letterbox, with your name on it.
Write what you like, to whoever you like. No ready-made answers.
The next letter takes into account what you wrote. And it makes you wait.

receive.title: In your letterbox, among the bills, there’s a letter for you.
receive.body: You open it standing in the kitchen. Someone is asking for your help, and knows your name. From then on, every time you walk past the letterbox, you look inside.
itemBodies: Stamped, postmarked, addressed to you. To be opened by hand.
Real paper and the voice of whoever is writing. To reread, to keep.
Telegrams and newspaper clippings, when the story speeds up.
The best part. You don’t know when the next one arrives.
receive.quote: “I didn’t think I’d actually wait for the next letter.”
receive.quoteSource: A reader from the first test
receive.giftNote: A present that doesn’t end on the 25th: it keeps arriving.

engine.title: How does a story write back?
engine.body: Every letter you write moves something. The characters remember what you told them, react, sometimes lie. Try it: this is the first letter of a story.
engine.letterText: I found a key in my father’s drawer. It opens no door in our house. You knew him better than I did: what should I do?
engine.replyEmpty: Pick a reply and watch which road the story takes.
replies: I went down last night. Behind the bottles there is a door I had never seen. The key turns. I didn’t have the courage to open it alone.
I asked her at dinner. She put down her fork and said: “That key should have been burned.” Then she didn’t speak again.
I put it back, as you said. This morning the drawer was empty. Someone else in this house knows about the key.
engine.timelineAria: Diagram of the story: one letter leads to three different roads, which meet again at a twist written by the author and continue towards the ending.
engine.timelineCaption: Three replies, three roads. But the twist and the ending were written by an author: you get there anyway, in your own way.
engine.demoNote: Here you pick one of three replies. In the real story you write whatever you want.
pointTitles: Every character has a mind of their own
pointBodies: No options A, B, C. Ask questions, accuse, comfort, change the subject: the story follows you.
Each one knows only what they lived through and what you wrote to them. Tell one a secret, and the others don’t know it.
The beginning, the twists and the endings are written by a person. Nobody lives the same story as you, but every one makes sense.
engine.ctaTitle: The first letter is only waiting for your address.

startMode.fixed: Fixed date (story always starts on the configured date)

hints.personality: Free JSON: traits, speech_pattern, letter_format, techniques…
hints.hiddenAgenda: Secret. Players never see this; only the AI Game Master and this character use it.
hints.openingLetter: Sent automatically when a game starts. Never write the date inside the letter — dates are shown by the platform.
hints.knownBy: Which characters know this fact. Nobody selected + not public = secret only the Game Master knows.
hints.conditions: JSON flags that must match the game state, e.g. {"victim_saved": true}.
hints.firstLetterLegacy: Old single opening letter. Prefer per-character opening letters below; this is used only if no character has one.
